claims.statement: Pinned macOS limits state GitHub-provided actions compatible with arm64, community actions may require manual runtime installation; nested virtualization unsupported; no Azure private networking/static IP on macOS larger runners. arm64 lacks static UUID/UDID while Intel has public static UDID4203018E-580F-C1B5-9525-B745CECA79EB; development provisioning depends on same-host testing and Apple account setup. GHEC condition includes residency restriction, not actual signing approval.
macOS runners unavailable on data-residency-site subdomains in pinned guidance; example domain is variable, not an inspected tenant.
Workflow tutorial creates .github/workflows/YOUR_WORKFLOW.yml with chosen filename; source instruction is inert and not consumer repository mutation or valid workflow proof.

Matrix include example assigns Node14.x/prod/site-a and Node16.x/dev/site-b, then env SITE/DATACENTER from matrix.site/datacenter. Prose incorrectly says env: matrix.env, which the shown matrix does not define. Preserve mismatch; no deployment or npm execution.

For merge queues, required Actions checks and conditionally organization-required workflows need merge_group in addition to PR/push triggers; otherwise queue checks are absent and merge fails. Event is distinct, not covered automatically by push or pull_request.
Annotation message can associate with a repository file and optional position; annotation creation is not evidence of actual finding validity.

Annotation optional fields: title no default; file defaults .github; col starts at1 with no default; endColumn no default; line starts at1/default1; endLine default1. No required parameter or actual annotation emitted.
Enterprise provider migration has additional linked considerations; link does not complete migration review or authorize conversion.
Pinned source states minimum8vCPU/64GB memory for Actions in its enclosing instance context; do not apply instance hardware threshold to every workflow runner or claim current capacity.

Enabling Actions or Code Security increases instance CPU/memory at least25% for each listed feature over user-tier base requirements; source recommends monitoring and potentially more. Combined sizing method and actual estate capacity still need scope resolution.
Runner move procedure selects a runner and destination via Runner group; selection is not authorized move or verified changed access.
Environment creation enters name and configures; names case-insensitive, unique within repository and at most255 characters. No environment created or protection activated.

When a dotcom action is first used, its namespace is retired in the enterprise to prevent creating a matching local organization/repository for abuse. Parent platform applicability, actual retirement and behavior are unverified.
Larger-runner static public IP configuration checks Assign unique & static public IP address ranges then Save; prior macOS/Azure restrictions still apply and no native setting changed.
New environment is a creation UI step only, not proof of protection or approval to create.
When repository already has a workflow, New workflow starts another; UI navigation is not approved workflow installation.
Pinned AWS OIDC guidance says custom claims unsupported. This narrow provider limitation is not a universal inability to constrain standard claims or current live AWS verification.

Environment use in workflow/OIDC policy should add protection rules for security, e.g. branch/tag deployment and secret access restrictions. Recommendation is not evidence rules exist or effective cloud trust enforcement.

Cloud provider must reach instance OIDC discovery and JWKS endpoints at the two placeholder HOSTNAME token-service paths. Accessibility requirement is not authorization to expose endpoints or change provider trust.
Further-reading links cover reusable-workflow OIDC and self-hosted runners; linked full bodies remain separate review work.
